Calcifying Epithelial Odontogenic Tumor: Radiographic examination: 3 cm unicystic radiolucent area with clear boundaries
Epithelium form: whorled masses of spindle cells, sheets, and plexiform strands
Calcification: sometimes seen and may be extensive

top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The presence of a unicystic radiolucent area with clear boundaries, whorled masses of spindle cells, and calcification are consistent with Calcifying Epithelial Odontogenic Tumor. Additionally, the absence of root apex resorption supports this diagnosis.

The association with an unerupted tooth and the presence of a unicystic radiolucent area are consistent with Adenomatoid Odontogenic Tumor. However, the presence of calcification and whorled masses of spindle cells are more characteristic of Calcifying Epithelial Odontogenic Tumor.
